raw_text:
This is uncomplicated, nonsevere unilateral acute otitis media (AOM): bulging TM plus effusion and acute otalgia; fever is below 39°C and pain is <48 hours.

I would offer shared-decision observation with reliable 48–72-hour follow-up, rather than mandate antibiotics today. At age 24 months, with unilateral nonsevere AOM and a well-appearing child, this is guideline-concordant. AAP guideline
, CDC outpatient guidance

Analgesia now and scheduled/as-needed for the first 24–48 h:

Acetaminophen 160 mg PO q4–6h PRN (5 mL of 160 mg/5 mL); max 5 doses/24 h.

Or ibuprofen 100 mg PO q6–8h PRN (5 mL of 100 mg/5 mL), appropriate given age and good hydration.

Use an oral syringe; avoid OTC cough/cold products. AAP medication guidance

Provide a safety-net prescription or arrange reassessment if pain/fever worsens at any point or is not clearly improving by 48–72 hours:

Amoxicillin 90 mg/kg/day divided BID × 7 days = 558 mg/dose BID for 12.4 kg.

Practical prescription: amoxicillin suspension 400 mg/5 mL: 6.5 mL PO BID × 7 days (520 mg/dose; ~84 mg/kg/day; dispense 100 mL). This uses a currently available 400 mg/5 mL formulation. AAP dosing/duration reference
, DailyMed formulation

If choosing immediate treatment because follow-up is uncertain or parent preference favors it, the same amoxicillin regimen is appropriate. Use amoxicillin-clavulanate instead only if amoxicillin in the preceding 30 days, purulent conjunctivitis, or recurrent AOM unresponsive to amoxicillin.

Return urgently for toxic appearance, dehydration, postauricular erythema/swelling or ear displacement, persistent high fever, new otorrhea, facial weakness, or worsening pain. No imaging, labs, or routine post-treatment ear check is needed if symptoms resolve.
